title: Why he never worked with Duke
summary: Contracts with Raymond Scott and a 52nd Street club kept him from joining Ellington, and club owners paid by name value.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: -- nobody was hearing anything about him until Duke brought him doing these things. I regret that I never worked with Duke, and I had a chance to work with him once. But I -- when he wanted me I couldn't get away. I was tied up. I was tied up around New York at that time. I had some contractual things going. I couldn't get away from. And I told him that I really want to work with him though.
When was that that he wanted you?

This was during the time I was on 52nd Street. But I had signed several contracts. I had a contract then with Raymond Scott on those radio broadcasts he was doing, and I had one in the club. You know, like on 52nd street when you worked in a club, if you worked in a band like Tiny Grimes band, you really didn't work for Tiny, you worked for Chick Gorman, the guy who ran the club. And if he figured you had a little name, well, he would give you a little more money. You know, sometimes you'd be making more money than the leader. And he'd sign you to a little six month deal or something, but not too tied up.
